summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for severe diffuse abdominal pain and nausea following a recent gastrostomy tube change, with a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and prior anastomotic ulcer. She was initially kept NPO, then advanced to a stage 3 diet as symptoms improved. A CT scan showed no obstruction, internal hernia, or tube misplacement. Pain was well controlled with oxycodone, and she tolerated tube feedings. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable throughout. At discharge, she was ambulatory, pain-controlled, and able to manage oral and tube medications. She was discharged home with instructions to continue sucralfate, avoid NSAIDs, and follow up with surgery. No complications occurred during the stay.
